title: What the ZPA Terraform provider sends, keeps and cleans up for application segments and their associations
aliases: terraform zpa app segment extranet false

prose.text: ZPA application segments come in four kinds (main, browser access, inspection, PRA), each with its own Terraform resource and SDK package. All four update by sending a full struct rebuilt from Terraform arguments, so what the schema cannot express goes out as Go zero values. The omitempty clears themselves are in [[shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes]]; this subject covers what is specific to segments and the objects hanging off them.

parent-flags-always-serialized.statement: The SDK request structs for the four application segment kinds declare some API flags without `omitempty`, so they are always in the request body, as false when the caller leaves them unset: `extranetEnabled`, `apiProtectionEnabled`, `autoAppProtectEnabled` and `adpEnabled` on the main segment; `extranetEnabled`, `apiProtectionEnabled` and `bypassOnReauth` on browser access; `extranetEnabled` and `apiProtectionEnabled` on inspection and PRA.

parent-flags-never-set.statement: The four resources build the request from Terraform arguments and never assign the unmodeled flags: the main segment expander sets `APIProtectionEnabled` and `BypassOnReauth` but not `ExtranetEnabled`, `AutoAppProtectEnabled` or `ADPEnabled`; the browser access expander sets none of its three; the inspection and PRA expanders set neither `ExtranetEnabled` nor `APIProtectionEnabled`. The schemas have no matching arguments to read.
parent-flags-never-set.conditions: Absence claim. Searched with `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zpa grep -n -i -E 'extranetenabled|autoappprotect|adpenabled|apiprotectionenabled|bypassonreauth' <ref> -- zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment.go zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_browser_access.go zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_inspection.go zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_pra.go` at v4.4.10 and HEAD. Hits are limited to the assignments quoted here and to reads from the API response (`resp.BypassOnReauth` and similar). The same files were read at both refs; the provider files are unchanged between them.

main-update-builds-from-state.statement: The main application segment update builds its whole request from Terraform arguments. It reads the existing segment only to detect that it is gone, and ignores any other error from that read, discards the result, and sends the rebuilt struct as the PUT body. The SDK's `Update` sends the struct it is given and merges nothing.

pra-update-sends-remote-values.statement: On a PRA segment update, every nested app whose domain already exists remotely is rebuilt from the remote object (name, enabled, port, protocol, connection security, domain, description). The configured values for that app are used only to decide whether its domain is still present. Only apps with a new domain are taken from the configuration. A change to an existing app's port, protocol, connection security, name or description is therefore not sent.

main-resource-unsupported-for-appprotect.statement: The `zpa_application_segment` resource documents that a segment on which Auto App Protection or Active Directory Inspection has been enabled, for example in the Admin Portal, becomes an inspection segment that only `zpa_application_segment_inspection` supports: it must be imported there and removed from `zpa_application_segment`, because any update the main resource applies disables the feature and leaves the per-domain inspection configuration invalid. Issue #687 reported that an unrelated update did exactly that and also made the segment vanish from the console's main list; it was closed as completed on 2026-10-01 with a reply from a member of the repository's organization, signed Zscaler DevRel, naming `zpa_application_segment_inspection` and its `trust_untrusted_cert` setting as the supported way to manage such a segment.

api-app-segment-put-semantics.title: How ZPA treats false, empty-object and duplicate-ID members in application segment PUTs
api-app-segment-put-semantics.blocks: saying whether the wire values above clear, keep or reject remote state
api-app-segment-put-semantics.detail: The client sends false for unmodeled flags, hidden false, zeroed nested-app flags, empty association objects, and in one path an ID shared by two entries. No captured source says what ZPA does with each. Test in a scratch tenant: enable a flag outside Terraform, apply an unrelated change, and re-read the segment; repeat with a hidden clientless app and with an inspection nested app that has options enabled.

api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules.title: Whether the v1 policy listing returns rules written through the v2 endpoints
api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules.blocks: saying whether the main segment delete cleanup reaches APP operands in rules created through the v2 resources
api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules.detail: The main cleanup lists rules with the v1 policy controller only. Create a rule with a v2 resource that has an APP operand for a test segment, then list the policy type through the v1 call and check whether the rule and operand appear.

segment-group-applications-drift.title: Whether a segment group applications list in a different order from the API's plans an update on every run
segment-group-applications-drift.detail: Unverified legacy statement (operator field observation from production Terraform use): segment group membership is managed from the application segment side, and carrying the applications list on the segment group in Terraform configuration produces phantom drift. From v4.4.14 the code settles membership changes: a membership change fails the plan instead of drifting. Still open: the plan-time check ignores order, but applications is a list that Read fills in the API's order, so whether a configuration listing the current applications in another order plans an in-place update on every run is not shown; the changelog says such configurations keep working without changes. The legacy drift on versions before v4.4.14 is also unreproduced. Plan twice with the applications listed in an order different from the API's.
